newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says foreign firms eyeing phosphate deposit.
newsitem.headline: Peru says foreign firms eyeing phosphate deposit.

text.p: Various U.S., Canadian and Mexican companies are interested in the upcoming privatization of Peru's state-owned Bayovar phosphate deposit, the government said Monday.
State news agency Andina added that Bayovar, in the northern department of Piura, was "one of the of the world's most important phosphate deposits" with total reserves of 372 million tonnes.
It did not name the companies showing interest, or say what the deposit's base price would be.

Last week, state miner Minero Peru announced it would restart its privatization process with the auction of the Bayover phosphate deposit in February. The company said it would receive offers for the deposit on February 11.

Minero Peru officials also confirmed plans to sell the Michiquillay copper and gold deposit, in Cajamarca department, and the Winicocha gold deposit, in Cuzco department, in the first quarter of 1997.
In the second half of 1997, the company, which began privatizing in 1993, will offer its Las Bambas copper deposit in Apurimac department and its anthracite coal deposit in La Libertad department.
The Minero Peru sales will run parallel to the ongoing, piecemeal privatization of the government's operating mining company, Centromin.
While Centromin's privatization program includes operating assets as well as deposits, Minero Peru will only sell off deposits.
